# Vendored zstd (decompress only)

`zstddeclib.c` is upstream zstd **1.5.7**, generated by facebook/zstd's own
`build/single_file_libs/create_single_file_decoder.sh`. Decompressor only — a device never
compresses — which keeps it to one file and a small binary. Pinned to 1.5.7 to match
`zstd-jni:1.5.7-4` on Android, so both platforms decode frames from the same encoder version.

Licensed BSD-3-Clause or GPLv2 at your option; this project selects BSD-3-Clause (`LICENSE`).

## Why vendored rather than the `libzstd` pod

Apple's Compression framework has no zstd, so iOS needs a decoder from somewhere. The plan
originally chose the `libzstd` CocoaPod. Checking it before shipping:

- owned by an individual, not Meta;
- one published version, **1.5.5**, last pushed **2023-11-22**;
- therefore cannot match Android's 1.5.7, and has no demonstrated CVE response.

For a library that verifies Ed25519 signatures and AES-GCM tags before executing downloaded code,
depending on a stale single-maintainer republish is a worse position than compiling the upstream
source we pin ourselves. The other alternative — a second codec for iOS only — costs ~29% larger
payloads, two code paths, and complicates the planned bytecode deltas.

## Why the symbols are renamed

`zstd_symbol_prefix.h` renames every global symbol this decoder defines to `DashOtaZ_*`. It is
generated — run `npm run gen:zstd-prefix` after updating the amalgamation — and the podspec
force-includes it when compiling C.

This is not cosmetic. Pods usually link **statically**, and if the host app also links a libzstd,
both copies define the same global `ZSTD_*` names. On Apple's static-link model that does not
reliably produce a duplicate-symbol error: the linker can satisfy our calls from the *other*
archive, so the decoder we pinned and tested is not necessarily the one that runs, and two zstd
builds are ABI-compatible enough to link while differing inside.

Visibility flags do not solve this. `-fvisibility=hidden` controls who may *see* a symbol, not what
it is *called*; the name stays global in the object file. Only renaming makes the copy private.

One wrinkle the generator handles: upstream does `#define ZSTD_isError ERR_isError` for inlining and
then `#undef ZSTD_isError` before defining the real function — which drops our macro with it. That
one is declared with an `__asm__` label instead, which is not a macro and survives. If a future
version `#undef`s another name we rename, `npm run gen:zstd-prefix` fails and says so.

`npm run lint:native` compiles this file exactly as the podspec does and fails if any un-prefixed
global symbol escapes.

## Verifying coexistence by hand

To prove a real libzstd and this copy can share one binary:

```sh
cc -c -O1 -w -include zstd_symbol_prefix.h zstddeclib.c -I. -o /tmp/ours.o
# link /tmp/ours.o together with -lzstd, compress with the system library, decompress with
# DashOtaZ_ZSTD_decompress, and compare the bytes.
```

Done on 2026-09-10 against Homebrew's libzstd: linked with no duplicate-symbol error, and the
prefixed decoder correctly read a frame the system library produced.

## Updating

Re-run the upstream generator against the new tag, replace `zstddeclib.c`, `zstd.h` and
`zstd_errors.h`, then `npm run gen:zstd-prefix`, then `npm run lint:native`. Do not hand-edit these
files.
